from the build scripts: a checker derived from the builder only ever proves

(X=1.0, Y=1.0 flow, Z=0.30 tall) is written here as [1.0, 0.30, 1.0].

RN-1563 to RN-1565, THE SE FORM PASS, and this is the raise in this wave
that needs the most argument, because a belt is the most numerous object
in a factory: portcost's reference base carries 57 of them against 22
smelters and no assembler at all. lod0 200 to 360 (actual 340), total 420
to 610 (actual 568), max_materials 4 to 5.
WHAT THE TRIANGLES BOUGHT, and they all went to one place. The only part
of a belt tile a player can ever see is the two 1.00 x 0.30 rail faces on
the cell edge, the deck from above, and the 0.10 m gap between one
under-frame and the next. Each rail was ONE extruded box. It is now a
fabricated section: flanges on the edge, a 15 mm lightening pocket
between them, a mid-span stiffener and solid full-section end blocks,
plus the splice plate and bolts a modular tile joins its neighbour with.
+192 tris x 57 belts is +10,944 against the reference base's 660,385,
i.e. +1.66 per cent of the whole scene, spent on the object the player
watches cargo ride along all game.
THE POCKET IS 15 mm BECAUSE CASCADE 0 IS 15.47 mm PER TEXEL. LOD1 is
still one solid box per rail, every new LOD0 vertex is within one shadow
texel of it, and all three cascades keep drawing the 108-triangle proxy
instead of promoting the 340-triangle mesh. A deeper pocket would have
looked no different and cost cascade 0 the whole LOD0 on every belt.
THE TILE ENDS STAY SOLID FULL-SECTION so a straight tile butted against a
curve has the same seam it always had: belt_curve_common.py shares this
file's rail width and deck height precisely so that junction is
invisible, and its rail is still one solid arc band.

W11 lane A, 2026-07-27. Four wearable slots: head, chest, legs, feet.
THE NODE NAMES ARE SLOT NAMES, NOT SET NAMES. A second armour set is a
second .glb carrying the same four node names, so the client's slot
lookup is set-independent and swapping a set is swapping a file. That
is the whole reason this file is not called armour_tier1.
SKINNED, NOT BONE-PARENTED. Each slot is a skinned mesh carrying the
SAME 44-bone armature as player_body.glb, the same bone names, the same
order and the same T-pose rest, all read from rig_common.BODY_BONES
rather than retyped. So a leg plate bends at the knee, a chest plate
rides the spine, and the client binds each slot to the skeleton it
already has instead of parenting twenty rigid props to twenty bones.
bones[] and rest_pose below are what make that a checked property and
not a hope: if the two rigs ever drift, this file fails.
pivot_mode 'none': an armour piece hangs at its own bone's height, so
a helmet's base is at y = 1.50 and a ground pivot is meaningless. Same
reasoning as the first-person arms.
tolerance_m 0.02, not 0.005, and for the same reason the view model has
it: armour has no footprint, no grid and no mating plane. Its envelope
is a did-it-explode bound. The fit that actually matters is armour
against the body surface, and that is judged by rendering the two
together, which is what a bounding box cannot do.

CraterFloor: biome.h classifies the moon by elevation band alone,

Regolith     RockSmall, RockLarge, RegolithRipple
MoonHighland HighlandOutcrop, RockLarge, RockSmall
CraterFloor  CraterRimRock, ImpactGlass, RockSmall

deliberately contains no live tree because both live trees in the
forest are harvest nodes; this atlas is the way a forest gets a

chop. The rule the game stated in words was enforced here as
geometry: harvest trees are small and branched to the ground
(TreeConifer 2.40 x 2.40 x 6.50, TreeBroadleaf 4.00 x 4.00 x 5.00);

The fractions the trees happen to measure today, for the record and

FOUR MATERIALS, pinned Bark / LeafDeep / Leaf / LeafLight on every

client, so this atlas costs ZERO additional draw calls; a fifth role
would cost one draw in the near pass plus one per shadow cascade.

crossed-quad impostor the harvest trees carry: there is no texture

rectangle, and LOD2 is the tree from 150 m to 500 m where nearly

Nothing collides.
18 to 42 tris each, NOT the 60 to 400 the biome props run at.
Built as tapered blade geometry, not alpha-tested crossed quads:
there is no texture pipeline and an untextured crossed quad renders
as a solid rectangle standing in the grass (spec correction, see
ASSET-SPECS 3.2).
THE VESSEL PART CATALOGUE (DW-29), and the TWO-CLASS STACK CONTRACT.
Twenty-three parts in one file, one group node each, so a renderer
clones the PART and gets its meshes, its sockets and its proxy
together.
TWO DIAMETER CLASSES AND NO MORE. Class S is 1.25 m (R 0.625, 16
segments) and class L is 2.50 m (R 1.250, 24 segments), exactly 2x.
A segment count divisible by 4 puts vertices on +-X and +-Y, so the
exported AABB is exactly the class diameter; a 14-gon at R 0.625
measures 1.250 x 1.244 and misses by 6 mm.
Seventeen stack parts are ground-pivoted on their bottom mating
plane, so socket_stack_bottom is always the origin and stacking is
one addition per part, with no per-part offset table anywhere.
StackAdapter is the ONE part whose two ends differ in class: bottom
L, top S. Without it two classes would be two disjoint catalogues.
Six radial parts (radial decoupler, vernier, fin, RCS, leg, solar
panel) have their origin on their MOUNT PLANE with the body
extending +X, which is neither 'ground' nor 'centre': pivot 'none'
and the dimensions are the check.
SolidBooster is carried radially but is NOT a radial part: it is a
stack part with a socket_radial_attach on its own hull, which mates
with RadialDecoupler's socket_radial_out. Same anti-parallel dot
product as a stack mate, so one rule covers both.
The landing leg and the solar panel are authored STOWED, because the
exported static pose is frame 1 of the deploy clip and a vessel
flies stowed. Each splits into a fixed mesh and an animated one,
because one Blender Action drives one object.
part_sockets is the real gate here: twenty parts carry a
socket_stack_top between them, so a flat presence check proves
nothing. It asserts each socket is under ITS part and lands on the
declared point in three.js axes.
LOD0 only, deliberately: a vessel is either near you or it is a
scaled-scene impostor, and there is no middle band for a part.

and PRICED rather than waved at. The multiplier is the whole
argument: VesselView and VabView each clone a PER-PART mesh and

mast on one edge, and the trench must NOT be filled in by the deck
proxy or the player walks on air over it. Five of them are the

in the world, the Cinder outpost beat, so +2,402 triangles is
0.09 percent of the 2.7M alert ceiling even if every one of them
were also drawn in all three shadow cascades. LOD1 356 and LOD2 184

TIER 2, GEOMETRY ONLY: the shader is the rendering domain's.
A UNIT plume, 1.00 m across the mouth and 1.00 m long, pointing down
three.js +Z, which is what a socket's facing is. So it attaches with

(exitDiameter, exitDiameter, plumeLength).

pivot 'none'.

reads the way this comment says it does.

culled as authored: DOUBLE_SIDED is palette-wide, and adding
EmissiveState to it would double-side every machine's state chip.
TIER 2, the scaled far-scene body. A UNIT icosphere at three
subdivision levels: 1280 / 320 / 80 triangles.
RADIUS COMES FROM BodyParams, never from the mesh. The renderer
scales by radiusM (Forge 600 km, Cinder 200 km, orbital.h), so one
mesh serves every body and dims are [2, 2, 2] by definition.
Icosphere, not UV sphere: a UV sphere pinches half its vertices into
the poles, which is exactly where a polar orbit flies over.
The mesh is INSCRIBED: every vertex is on radius 1.0, so every face
sags below it by 0.45% at LOD0, 1.78% at LOD1 and 6.58% at LOD2. A
renderer that needs the horizon exact scales by radiusM * (1 + sag).
pivot 'centre': a body is positioned by its centre, not stood on the
ground. One material; the renderer recolours base colour per body.
TIER 0 BASE BUILDING, the deck family. Module 1 x 1 x 0.50 m.
ANCHOR: a CELL CENTRE, floor(x) + 0.5, exactly like a 1x1 machine.
The parts list checks LOD1 and LOD2 on the same box as LOD0, because
a tiling part whose far LOD is a different size shows a seam opening
up as the player walks away, and the single lod0_node check would
never see it.

not by the plan module: 4 x 4 x 0.50 is the same 8:1 slab a 1 m deck
was at 2:1, and scaling it would have given a 2 m plinth.
The storey pitch identity DECK_H + WALL_H = STOREY = 4.00 m is
asserted in structure_common.py, and STOREY now EQUALS CELL, so the
plan lattice and the vertical lattice are one 4 m number.
TIER 0 BASE BUILDING. The SAME 4 x 4 x 0.50 m envelope as the
foundation, deliberately: a deck of two thicknesses would give the
storey pitch two values.
THIS PART IS ALSO THE CEILING. There is no ceiling.glb; storey N's
ceiling is storey N+1's floor at z = 4(N+1), same part, same origin.
That is why the ribs are underneath and the plate on top.
TIER 0 BASE BUILDING, the wall family. Module 4.00 wide x 0.25 thick
x 3.50 m tall.
ANCHOR: a CELL EDGE MIDPOINT, not a cell centre. The panel is centred
on its own origin across the thickness (which is what the ground
pivot check asserts), so putting that origin on the edge line makes
one wall serve both cells it divides and makes four walls close
exactly around one foundation.

reason DECK_H stays 0.50: a wall is as thick as a wall is, and a 1 m
thick partition is a bunker. Only the PLAN module scaled.
dims [4.0, 3.50, 0.25]: the 3.50 landing on three.js Y is what proves
export_yup fired, and it is the number that must equal STOREY - DECK_H.
TIER 0 BASE BUILDING. The wall module with a 1.20 x 2.40 m opening,
so it drops into any cell of any wall run with no special case.

decision (DW-32, BT-11). The MODULE scaled and the OPENING did not:
a 4 m opening is a garage, and a sub-cell door would need a second,
finer lattice for wall furniture that no part of the placement
system has. So the panel is 4 m and the hole in it is 1.20 m, which
is a double-leaf industrial doorway against a 0.60 m player.

game a player can walk around INSIDE. Built by

below is reasoned from what it is rather than copied from a neighbour.

Station_* is the pressure hulls and appendages; StationInt_* is the

from inside it, through a viewport or through the breach, so a client
drawing the station at range skips the interior with no hole in the
silhouette. The hull's INNER skin is the void ceiling, which is why
the two skins are one closed manifold and why the interior is a
separate node rather than a separate file.

otherwise be measured against is the part that is missing: dropping
it measured 940.86 mm.
THE HULL STEM IS NOT THERE YET AND THE NUMBER IS STATED RATHER THAN
ROUNDED OFF. Station_LOD1 measures 139.87 mm and Station_LOD2 278.37,
so LOD1 earns cascade 2 only and the hull's marginal multiplier is

causes were found and fixed by measurement (3,976.57 mm, 1,976.71,

A fifth remains unattributed. It is worth 3.0x against 2.0x on this

PIVOT IS `none`, WHICH IS THE HONEST OPTION AND NOT A FREE PASS. The
useful origin for a free-flying body is the spine axis at the hall
centre, which is the artificial-gravity datum and where a physics body
wants its frame. `centre` would demand the AABB centre land there to
5 mm, and the AABB is set by the solar wing tips, the docking collar
and the torn aft rim, so honouring it would force symmetric extents on
an asset whose brief is asymmetry. validate_glb.py prints `none (view
model)` for this branch, which is a stale message rather than a wrong
check; a `free` mode is flagged to Admin and is not taken mid-flight.
COLLISION IS THE FEATURE. 57 proxies, floors and walls and ceilings
authored separately because one enclosing box cannot describe an
interior and would make the station a solid lump. Three physics facts
govern the set: the walker can stand on a proxy with no new code
(KinematicBody already takes the higher of the terrain floor and
StructureBodies.deckUnder, measured 264 of 264 ticks grounded at 400
km); floors get an exact slab solve; and R48, THERE IS NO CEILING
AUTHORITY IN THE WALKER, only free() with three point samples 0.75 m
apart, so a horizontal proxy thinner than 0.75 m fits between two
samples and the player passes clean through it. Every overhead proxy
here is therefore 0.80 m thick against a 0.12 m visible ceiling panel,
which is a proxy being coarser than what it stands for, exactly as a
machine's box proxy is coarser than its hull. The whole set comes out
of one function, `collision_boxes()`, so the philosophy can change
without a rendered triangle moving.
NO ROTATING HABITAT RING is walkable, and that is a form decision
taken from a physics constraint rather than a style preference. Down
is the planet radial, derived per tick from the feet, and deckUnder
solves where a line through the planet centre exits a box, so the
parameter it returns IS a radius. A non-radial up breaks it outright
along with climbGate, slopeGate, escapeRock and the voxel collider.
The station holds nadir attitude and gets real inverse-square gravity
for nothing.
THE RUIN: an ancient civilisation's temple platform, destroyed long ago,
and the first thing story_line_outline_v1.txt sends the player to walk to.
Built by tools/blender/build_ruin.py on station_form.py and
machine_form.py, on structure_common.CELL's 4.00 m module.
EVERY DIMENSION IS DERIVED FROM core/include/of/poi.h AND NOT CHOSEN.
forgeSpecs publishes footprintM 18.0, maxTiltDeg 4.0, maxResidM 1.0 and
variants 1, and poi.h then does the arithmetic itself in prose: the worst
admissible ground drops 18*tan(4) = 1.2587 m from centre to rim and
carries up to 1.0 m of residual, so a ruin needs 2.2587 m of plinth,
skirt or buried course at its rim with no daylight under it. Nothing
levels terrain under a static structure, so that is a requirement on the
MESH. The platform is a 24-gon, R 17.60 m buried and 17.12 m at the
stylobate, so a 35.20 m complex inside an 18.00 m footprint gate.
THE PIVOT IS `ground` AND socket_grade IS WHAT MAKES THAT POSSIBLE. Read
naively the two requirements contradict: `ground` puts the model's lowest
vertex on y = 0 and FSite.pos is a SURFACE point, which would leave the
buried course nowhere to be, because the rim ground is up to 2.26 m LOWER
than the centre. The asset resolves it by publishing its own datum
instead of borrowing the pivot's: z = 0 is the bottom of the buried
course (so `ground` is satisfied exactly and the pivot check is real) and
socket_grade at y = 2.30 is the plane the placement lane puts on
FSite.pos, i.e. the model is SUNK 2.30 m relative to the surface point.
On flat ground the whole course is invisible, which is what a buried
course is; on the worst ground the gate admits the rim ground falls to
y = 0.04 and the course still reaches below it, with 40 mm to spare and
no tuning. The datum is a socket rather than a comment because a
relationship written in prose is a number nobody is checking, and the
socket_frames block below is the check.
`ground` ALSO DEMANDS A CENTRED AABB, WHICH FIGHTS ART-DIRECTION.md's
ASYMMETRY, and the fight is settled by deciding which element owns the
bounding box. The buried course is a plain 24-gon prism, exactly centred,
and it is the widest thing on the asset by 140 mm; everything above it is
asserted at build time to stay inside R_KEEP, so settlement, spall, tilt
and collapse are all inward and downward and none of them can reach the
AABB. The only symmetric element is therefore the one that is buried on
every site the gate admits, and the asymmetry lives entirely in what a
player can see. Measured: centre x = z = 0.000000, base y = 0.000000.

360.05  a real HOLE in the door wall: the jambs stopped at the lintel

269.43  the stylobate skin on one shared Shell at the nominal radius,

207.16  spall and moss SAMPLED inside a window and then SIZED past it,

hard rectangular outline, flat contrasting colour, reading as signage
stuck to the stone rather than as damage in it. `clean is now a defect`

second smaller box on the layer BELOW, offset about a third of the main

roughly halved, so the same triangles buy half as many marks each of

EVERY WEAR MARK HAS A CAUSE AND THE CAUSES ARE FIELDS, NOT DECALS.
damage(x, y) is one falloff from a point off the +X / -Y quarter and it
decides pier state, blackening, rubble placement and spall depth, so the
+X / -Y corner is flattened, the -X / +Y side stands, and the surviving
colonnade is contiguous (which is what lets an entablature exist at all:

cornice and nowhere else, so where the cornice is broken the stain stops
dead. shade() is a dot product against one authored sun bearing, and
inside the cella the only growth is the one patch under the hole in the
roof, because that is the only place light and water both arrive.
sag_beam bows the architrave's own soffit over its span rather than
rotating a straight block, which is the difference between a beam that
has crept and one that has not.

station_form.antenna EXISTS AND WAS REFUSED, which is worth recording
because reuse is the default rule. It is a mast box plus a fan of
eight ONE-SIDED triangles round a cone, correct for a 400 km hull
silhouette the player flies past. It has no thickness, no rim, no
ribs, no feed and no mount, and because OF_SteelLight is backface
culled it renders as a hole in the world when seen from behind - which
is roughly half the time a player walks round a thing standing on the
ground. The reflector here is a CLOSED solid (front skin, back skin,
outer rim, inner rim) wound by mf.oriented off the signed volume.
THE FOUR ANCHORS OWN THE BOUNDING BOX AND THAT IS WHY THERE ARE FOUR.
The `ground` pivot wants a centred AABB and ART-DIRECTION.md wants
asymmetry; the ruin gives the box to its buried course and the
research station to its skid deck. Four identical anchor blocks at
four corners is not a compromise with the validator, it is what a
guyed mast IS, and it buys everything else the freedom to be
lopsided: the equipment cabinet is on one side only, the feeder
climbs one chord only, the rungs are on one face only, and the dish
hangs entirely into the -Y half. The blocks are 0.44 square at
(+-1.28, +-1.28) so their outer faces land on +-1.50 exactly, and
everything else is asserted inside KEEP = 1.42. THE YELLOW IS
STRUCTURE, a capping course rather than paint: the first build used
`scribe` stripes on the outboard faces, which stood 6 mm proud (AABB
3.006) and, being below LOD1's threshold, would have given the three
tiers DIFFERENT bounding boxes. The anchor bolts moved from 0.15 to
0.11 off centre for the same reason.
HEIGHT IS SOLVED BACKWARDS. The topmost point of the asset is the
reflector rim at the top of the bowl, (DISH_R + DEPTH) * sin(45) above
the vertex, so TRUNNION_Z = 6.00 - that, = 5.0255. Both LOD sector
counts (16 and 8) put a vertex at exactly theta = 90 degrees, which is
what lets all three tiers share one dims_xyz_m. The dish is f/D 0.40
(focal 0.840 m, depth 0.3281 m) and is aimed at -Y, i.e. AT the player
who placed it and over their head, because ResearchStations.faceToward
turns glTF +Z (Blender -Y) toward the eye and a dish facing away would
show its back for ever.
THE PICK SPHERE DOES NOT REACH THE HEAD, MEASURED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.
Antennas.pick is ResearchStations.pick verbatim - a 1.40 m sphere
0.70 m up, plus 0.50 m of slack - so it refuses any ray whose
perpendicular distance from (0, 0, 0.70) exceeds 1.90 m. On the 2.44 m
bench that is satisfiable and the build asserts it vertex by vertex;
on a 6 m mast it is not, and satisfying it would mean building a
2.6 m antenna. MEASURED: 57.0 per cent of LOD0 vertices lie inside
the sphere and on the mast axis selection stops at z = 2.555. What
this means in play is that a LEVEL crosshair at eye height 1.60 m
scores |1.60 - 0.70| = 0.90 m against the 1.90 m limit at any range,
so aiming at the tower works and aiming at the dish does not. The
borrowed power_pole.glb had the identical property at 4.0 m and
nobody had measured it. Widening ANTENNA_RADIUS_M is a gameplay
change and is left to that lane rather than taken by an art lane.
THE LADDER. LOD1 takes min_layer `clip` 0.061, dropping every greeble
at or under `hinge` 0.052, and keeps the dish at 16 sectors:
check_shadow_lod.py measures 50.76 mm, so it earns cascades 1 and 2
and the marginal multiplier is 2.0x. LOD2 takes `bracket` 0.232 AND
three structural savings the layer ladder would refuse - the dish
drops to 8 sectors, half the tower diagonals go, the guy turnbuckles
go and the quadripod loses two legs. An 8-gon reflector sits
r(1 - cos(180/8)) = 80 mm inside a 16-gon one, so this tier CANNOT be
shadow-safe: it MEASURES 209.98 mm, which happens to fall just inside
cascade 2's 210.94 mm texel, and that is a coincidence rather than a
design and is not relied on anywhere. It is a screen-distance tier,
stated in advance rather than discovered afterwards, which is
build_ruin.py's own correction to build_space_station.py.
THE BUDGET. LOD0 measures 2,848 against a 3,200 cap and the three
tiers total 6,688 against 7,400. GP-536 makes the reveal idempotent
(of_poi_mark_known returning false), so a second antenna EXTENDS
coverage rather than double-counting and a player has a real reason
to build two or three across a base's spread - the simultaneous count
is one or two, not one. At the measured 2.0x marginal multiplier two
antennas cost 2 x (2,848 + 2 x 2,272) = 14,784 triangles against
RN-71's 555k to 1.0 M surface frame, 1.5 to 2.7 per cent. The lattice
is where the triangles went: 900 of LOD0's are the tower's chords,
ties and diagonals, and they are what stops it reading as a pole.
COLLISION IS SEVEN BOXES. Plinth, mast and cabinet plus one per
anchor: the anchors are 0.26 m and steppable against CAPSULE.stepUpM
1.10, but they are solid, because a guy anchor a player walks
through is the state in which nobody trusts any collider on the
asset. Naming is col_Anchor1..4 rather than col_Anchor_1..4 on
purpose: check-proxies.mjs catalogues the three.js `Name_<digits>`
trap, where a proxy genuinely named col_Step_1 silently deletes
col_Step_2 and everything after it.
EIGHT ROLES, ALL ALREADY IN of_lib.PALETTE AND IN ALL THREE TABLES
check-roles.mjs COMPARES, so this build opened no shared file. Steel
is the cabinet sheet, SteelDark every structural member, SteelLight
the reflector skin and the bright fittings, Accent the fascia and
placards, Hazard the anchor capping course, Rubber the feeder and
conduit, EmissiveState the obstruction light and the cabinet lamp,
and Copper is the two places a real installation is not painted
steel: the waveguide and feed collar, and the earth bonding braid.
Nothing here is double sided.
NO CLIPS, AND THAT IS A REFUSAL. A slowly rotating dish is the
obvious animation and nothing in the client would play it: Antennas.ts
clones the template, calls selectLod and never touches
AnimationMixer, and a declared clip that nothing drives is dead bytes
plus a row in this file that reads like a feature. The elevation
screw jack under the dish's back rib is the static version of the
same statement - it says the thing points somewhere - and it costs
two boxes.
